# Formula Collection {#sec-formulas}

This appendix collects the formulas of the script, ordered by task. It contains no explanations: what a formula means and when it applies is explained in the chapter named in the last column.

Notation: $x_1, \dots, x_n$ are observations, $n$ is the sample size, $\bar x$ the mean, $\tilde x$ the median and $s$ the sample standard deviation. $\sum_i$ runs over all observations.

## Describing data

| Quantity | Formula | Used in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mean | $\bar x = \dfrac{1}{n}\sum_i x_i$ | Ch. 2 |
| Sample standard deviation | $s = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{n-1}\sum_i (x_i - \bar x)^2}$ | Ch. 2 |
| Interquartile range | $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$ (quartiles: 25 % and 75 % quantiles) | Ch. 2 |
| Median absolute deviation | $\text{MAD} = \operatorname{median}\big(\lvert x_1 - \tilde x \rvert, \dots, \lvert x_n - \tilde x \rvert\big)$ | Ch. 2 |
| IQR rule (Tukey) | flag $x_i$ if $x_i < Q_1 - 1.5\,\text{IQR}$ or $x_i > Q_3 + 1.5\,\text{IQR}$ | Ch. 2 |
| Robust z-score | $z_i = \dfrac{x_i - \tilde x}{1.4826 \cdot \text{MAD}}$, flag $x_i$ if $\lvert z_i \rvert > 3.5$ | Ch. 2 |
| Pearson correlation | $r_{xy} = \dfrac{\sum_i (x_i - \bar x)(y_i - \bar y)}{\sqrt{\sum_i (x_i - \bar x)^2}\,\sqrt{\sum_i (y_i - \bar y)^2}}$ | Ch. 1 |

## Prediction errors

| Quantity | Formula | Used in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mean absolute error | $\text{MAE} = \dfrac{1}{n}\sum_i \lvert y_i - \hat y_i \rvert$ | Ch. 1 |
| Root mean squared error | $\text{RMSE} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{n}\sum_i (y_i - \hat y_i)^2}$ | Ch. 1 |

## Probability and lifetimes

| Quantity | Formula | Used in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Distribution function, density | $F(x) = P(X \le x)$, $\quad f(x) = F'(x)$ | Ch. 3 |
| Probability of an interval | $P(a < X \le b) = F(b) - F(a) = \int_a^b f(x)\,dx$ | Ch. 3 |
| Quantile | $F^{-1}(p)$: the value below which a share $p$ lies | Ch. 3 |
| Expected value, variance | $E[X] = \int x\,f(x)\,dx$, $\quad \text{Var}(X) = E\big[(X - E[X])^2\big]$ | Ch. 3 |
| Central limit theorem | $\bar X_n$ is approximately normal with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma/\sqrt{n}$ | Ch. 3 |
| Reliability (lifetime $X$) | $R(t) = 1 - F(t) = P(X > t)$ | Ch. 3 |
| Weibull distribution | $F(t) = 1 - \exp\left[-\left(\dfrac{t}{\eta}\right)^{\beta}\right]$ | Ch. 3 |
| Three-parameter Weibull | $F(t) = 1 - \exp\left[-\left(\dfrac{t - t_0}{\eta}\right)^{\beta}\right]$ for $t > t_0$, $\quad F(t) = 0$ for $t \le t_0$ | Ch. 3 |
| Hazard rate | $h(t) = \dfrac{f(t)}{R(t)}$; Weibull: $h(t) = \dfrac{\beta}{\eta}\left(\dfrac{t}{\eta}\right)^{\beta - 1}$ | Ch. 3 |
| B10 life (Weibull) | $B_{10} = \eta\,(-\ln 0.9)^{1/\beta}$ | Ch. 3 |
| Log-likelihood | $\ell(\theta) = \sum_i \ln f(x_i; \theta)$, maximised by the estimate $\hat\theta$ | Ch. 3 |
| Akaike information criterion | $\mathrm{AIC} = 2k - 2\,\ell(\hat\theta)$, $\quad k$ = number of fitted parameters | Ch. 3 |
| Bayes' theorem | $P(F \mid A) = \dfrac{P(A \mid F)\,P(F)}{P(A)}$, $\quad P(A) = P(A \mid F)\,P(F) + P(A \mid \bar F)\,P(\bar F)$ | Ch. 3, 7 |
| Bayes' theorem for densities | $p(\theta \mid y) \propto p(y \mid \theta)\,p(\theta)$: posterior ∝ likelihood × prior | Ch. 3, 6 |

## Confidence intervals

| Quantity | Formula | Used in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard error of the mean | $\text{SE} = \dfrac{s}{\sqrt n}$ | Ch. 3 |
| 95 % confidence interval for the mean | $\bar x \pm t_{n-1,\,0.975}\,\dfrac{s}{\sqrt n}$ | Ch. 3 |
| Bootstrap (percentile method) | 95 % interval: 2.5 % and 97.5 % quantiles of the bootstrap replicates | Ch. 3 |
| 95 % confidence interval for a regression coefficient | $\hat\beta_j \pm t_{n-p-1,\,0.975}\,\text{SE}(\hat\beta_j)$ | Ch. 5 |
| Standard error of a regression prediction | $\text{SE}(\hat y_0) = \hat\sigma\,\sqrt{x_0^\top (X^\top X)^{-1} x_0}$, $\quad \hat y_0 = x_0^\top \hat\beta$, $\quad x_0 = (1, x_{01}, \dots, x_{0p})^\top$ | Ch. 5 |
| 95 % confidence interval for the mean response | $\hat y_0 \pm t_{n-p-1,\,0.975}\,\text{SE}(\hat y_0)$ | Ch. 5 |
| 95 % prediction interval for a single new observation | $\hat y_0 \pm t_{n-p-1,\,0.975}\,\sqrt{\hat\sigma^2 + \text{SE}(\hat y_0)^2}$ | Ch. 5 |

## Hypothesis tests

| Quantity | Formula | Used in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Welch t-test | $t = \dfrac{\bar x_1 - \bar x_2}{\sqrt{s_1^2/n_1 + s_2^2/n_2}}$ | Ch. 4 |
| Degrees of freedom (Welch) | $\nu = \dfrac{\left(s_1^2/n_1 + s_2^2/n_2\right)^2}{\dfrac{(s_1^2/n_1)^2}{n_1 - 1} + \dfrac{(s_2^2/n_2)^2}{n_2 - 1}}$ | Ch. 4 |
| Range of $\nu$ | $\min(n_1, n_2) - 1 \le \nu \le n_1 + n_2 - 2$ | Ch. 4 |
| Cohen's d | $d = \dfrac{\bar x_1 - \bar x_2}{s_p}$, $\quad s_p = \sqrt{\dfrac{s_1^2 + s_2^2}{2}}$ | Ch. 4 |
| One-way ANOVA ($k$ groups, $N$ observations) | $F = \dfrac{\sum_j n_j(\bar x_j - \bar x)^2/(k-1)}{\sum_j \sum_i (x_{ij} - \bar x_j)^2/(N-k)}$ | Ch. 4 |
| Chi-squared test | $\chi^2 = \sum \dfrac{(O - E)^2}{E}$, $\quad E = \dfrac{\text{row total} \cdot \text{column total}}{\text{total count}}$ | Ch. 4 |
| False alarms in $m$ independent tests | $P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - (1 - \alpha)^m$ | Ch. 4 |
| Bonferroni correction | significance level $\alpha/m$ for each of $m$ tests | Ch. 4 |
| Sample size per group (two-sample t-test) | $n \approx \dfrac{2\,(z_{1-\alpha/2} + z_{1-\beta})^2}{d^2}$, $\quad d = \delta/\sigma$; $\quad n \approx 16/d^2$ for $\alpha = 0.05$ and power 0.8 | Ch. 4 |
| t-value of a regression coefficient | $t_j = \dfrac{\hat\beta_j}{\text{SE}(\hat\beta_j)}$, t-distribution with $n - p - 1$ degrees of freedom under $H_0: \beta_j = 0$ | Ch. 5 |

## Regression

| Quantity | Formula | Used in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Multiple linear regression | $y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_{i1} + \dots + \beta_p x_{ip} + \varepsilon_i$, $\quad \varepsilon_i \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$ independent | Ch. 5 |
| Least squares estimate | $\hat\beta = (X^\top X)^{-1} X^\top y$, $\quad \widehat{\text{Cov}}(\hat\beta) = \hat\sigma^2 (X^\top X)^{-1}$ | Ch. 5 |
| Residual variance | $\hat\sigma^2 = \dfrac{1}{n - p - 1}\sum_i (y_i - \hat y_i)^2$ | Ch. 5 |
| Coefficient of determination | $R^2 = 1 - \dfrac{\sum_i (y_i - \hat y_i)^2}{\sum_i (y_i - \bar y)^2}$ | Ch. 5 |
| Adjusted coefficient of determination | $R^2_{\text{adj}} = 1 - (1 - R^2)\,\dfrac{n - 1}{n - p - 1}$ | Ch. 5 |
| Variance inflation factor | $\text{VIF}_j = \dfrac{1}{1 - R_j^2}$, $\quad R_j^2$: $R^2$ of a regression that predicts $x_j$ from all other inputs | Ch. 5 |
| Nonlinear least squares | $\hat\theta = \arg\min_{\theta} \sum_i \big(y_i - f(x_i; \theta)\big)^2$ | Ch. 5 |

## Model selection and regularisation

| Quantity | Formula | Used in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bias–variance decomposition | $E\big[(y - \hat f(x))^2\big] = \big(E[\hat f(x)] - f(x)\big)^2 + \text{Var}\big(\hat f(x)\big) + \sigma^2$: bias² + variance + irreducible noise | Ch. 6 |
| k-fold cross-validation error | mean of the errors on the $k$ held-out folds, each computed with the model trained on the other $k - 1$ folds | Ch. 6 |
| Ridge regression | $\min_\beta \sum_i (y_i - x_i^\top\beta)^2 + \lambda \sum_j \beta_j^2$ | Ch. 6 |
| Lasso regression | $\min_\beta \sum_i (y_i - x_i^\top\beta)^2 + \lambda \sum_j \lvert\beta_j\rvert$ | Ch. 6 |
| Kernel (correlation of two inputs) | $\rho(x, x') = \exp\left(-\dfrac{(x - x')^2}{2\ell^2}\right)$, $\quad \ell$: length scale | Ch. 6 |
| Gaussian process, step 1: one measurement $y_1$ at $x_1$ | $\mu_1 = m + w\,(y_1 - m)$, $\quad \sigma_1 = \sigma_f\sqrt{1 - w}$, $\quad w = \dfrac{\sigma_f^2}{\sigma_f^2 + \sigma_n^2}$ | Ch. 6 |
| Gaussian process, step 2: other inputs $x$ | $\mu(x) = m + \rho\,w\,(y_1 - m)$, $\quad \sigma(x) = \sigma_f\sqrt{1 - \rho^2 w}$, $\quad \rho = \rho(x, x_1)$ | Ch. 6 |

## Classification

| Quantity | Formula | Used in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Logistic regression | $P(y = 1 \mid x) = \dfrac{1}{1 + e^{-(\beta_0 + \beta^\top x)}}$ | Ch. 7 |
| Bernoulli likelihood | $L = \prod_i p_i^{\,y_i}(1 - p_i)^{1 - y_i}$ | Ch. 3, 7 |
| Log-loss (cross-entropy, two classes) | $-\ln L = -\sum_i \big[y_i \ln p_i + (1 - y_i)\ln(1 - p_i)\big]$ | Ch. 7 |
| Softmax and cross-entropy ($K$ classes) | $p_k = \dfrac{e^{z_k}}{\sum_{j} e^{z_j}}$, $\quad -\sum_i \ln p_{i,\,\text{true class}}$ | Ch. 8 |
| Gini impurity | $G = 1 - \sum_k p_k^2$, $\quad p_k$: share of class $k$ in a node | Ch. 7 |
| Accuracy, precision, recall | $\dfrac{TP + TN}{\text{all}}$, $\quad \dfrac{TP}{TP + FP}$, $\quad \dfrac{TP}{TP + FN}$ | Ch. 7 |
| F1 score | $F_1 = \dfrac{2 \cdot \text{precision} \cdot \text{recall}}{\text{precision} + \text{recall}}$ | Ch. 7 |
| Cost-optimal threshold (calibrated probabilities) | $\dfrac{c_{FP}}{c_{FP} + c_{FN}}$ | Ch. 7 |
| Balanced accuracy | mean of the recalls of all classes | Ch. 7, 8 |

## Ensembles and interpretation

| Quantity | Formula | Used in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Average of $B$ predictions (variance $\sigma^2$, pairwise correlation $\rho$) | $\text{Var} = \rho\,\sigma^2 + \dfrac{1 - \rho}{B}\,\sigma^2$ | Ch. 8 |
| Gradient boosting | $F_m(x) = F_{m-1}(x) + \nu\,h_m(x)$, $\quad h_m$ fitted to the negative gradient of the loss; squared error: to the residuals $y_i - F_{m-1}(x_i)$ | Ch. 8 |
| Permutation importance of feature $j$ | score on test data minus score after randomly shuffling feature $j$ | Ch. 8 |

## Unsupervised learning

| Quantity | Formula | Used in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PCA scores of a standardised observation $z$ | $t = V_k^\top z$, $\quad V_k = [v_1, \dots, v_k]$: the first $k$ loadings | Ch. 9 |
| Share of variance explained by component $j$ | $\lambda_j / p$, $\quad \lambda_j$: variance of the scores of component $j$, $p$: number of standardised variables | Ch. 9 |
| Hotelling's T² | $T^2 = \sum_{j=1}^k \dfrac{t_j^2}{\lambda_j}$ | Ch. 9 |
| Squared prediction error | $\text{SPE} = \lVert z - V_k t \rVert^2$ | Ch. 9 |
| k-means | minimise $\sum_{c=1}^{k} \sum_{i \in c} \lVert x_i - \mu_c \rVert^2$, $\quad \mu_c$: centre (mean) of cluster $c$ | Ch. 9 |
